title: Informer: Sparse attention reduces the memory footprint of long-context forecasting on ETTh1, Electricity
abstract: We study long-horizon multivariate forecasting using Informer, a sparse-attention transformer with ProbSparse self-attention. On ETTh1, Electricity, at horizon 336, Sparse attention reduces the memory footprint of long-context forecasting on ETTh1, Electricity. Informer uses 13% less GPU memory than full-attention transformers at input length 1024. We discuss two limitations: Confidence intervals or standard errors are not reported for the headline metric. Missing-value handling is delegated to preprocessing and not stress-tested. Future work should address combining channel-independent tokenisation with variate-token attention. and reporting per-seed variance and confidence intervals for the headline metric.
